NGAI: Any of three Chinese surnames of Cantonese origin, used primarily in Hong Kong.
NGAIO: An evergreen tree of species Myoporum laetum, native to New Zealand.
NGANASAN: A member of a people who live in the extreme northwest of Siberia.
NGED: Initialism of National Grid Electricity Distribution.
NGEN: An East Santo language spoken on Espiritu Santo in Vanuatu.
NGERULMUD: The capital city of Palau in which the government offices are located.
NGO: A surname from Vietnamese [in turn from Hokkien].
NGON: A polygon with n sides, where n represents any integer greater than or equal to three; often used to represent a polygon
NGRAM: A contiguous sequence of one or more items (usually characters or words) from a given sequence of text or speech, used i
NGS: Abbreviation of nanograms plural of ng (“nanogramme”); Nonstandard form of ng (“nanogrammes”).
NGULTRUM: The official currency of Bhutan, equal to 100 chetrums.
NGUNI: The group of Southern African peoples comprising the Zulu, Xhosa, Swazi, Mpondo and Ndebele nations.
NGWEE: A currency of Zambia, one hundredth of a kwacha.
